Rejected Alternatives

An error or status code when a value is clamped. The ticket originally proposed returning an error code. A top-level error code other than NONE means that the request failed, and only the Streams heartbeat has a status list. A non-fatal status could be designed, but it would carry less information than ConfiguredValue: which configuration differs, and both values. A new code value in an existing field would also change the meaning of that field for older clients.

Only the configurations that can be clamped. An earlier version of this proposal covered the 15 configurations that can be clamped to broker bounds. The Motivation describes two problems: clients cannot see effective values, and cannot see when an override is not in effect. The first one applies to every group configuration, and the ticket asks for all of them. The generic list and the conditional sending remove most of the per-configuration and repeated costs that motivated the narrower scope.

Reporting share configurations in the share group heartbeat. The share configurations that govern record delivery (record lock duration, delivery count limit, maximum record locks, renew acknowledge, auto offset reset, isolation level and the dead letter queue settings) are applied by the partition leaders, not by the group coordinator. Each broker evaluates them against its own bounds and defaults. A value reported by the coordinator could therefore differ from the value a leader applies, so each value is reported by the broker that applies it.

A typed field per configuration. Typed fields would be checked by the schema and more compact on the wire, but every configuration would need its own fields and its own logging code, and every configuration added later would need a protocol change. The new information is used only for diagnostics, while the existing typed fields keep driving client behavior. A list with one entry structure lets the client handle all configurations the same way.

Tagged fields on the existing versions, without a new version. This is possible, and there are precedents (ApiVersionsResponse v3, FetchResponse v12). With a new version, the broker includes the fields only for requests at a version that defines them, and a client can tell an old broker from one that has nothing to report. Without it, both would need extra rules. For the request header, the discussion of KIP-1313 also moved from a tagged field alone to a new version with a tagged field.

Sending the full list in every response. This is the simplest option, but names and values would be repeated in every response. ShareFetch and ShareAcknowledge responses can be far more frequent than heartbeats.

The broker tracking what it sent to each member. A lost response would leave the broker believing that the client has the list, and a separate recovery rule would be needed.

An epoch instead of a content hash. A counter kept in memory restarts with the broker, so after a restart or a coordinator change it can reach the value a client still holds while the content differs. A pair of the broker's registration epoch and a per-group counter avoids this and has no collisions, but needs per-group state on every broker and a larger token. The content hash needs no state. Identical canonical snapshot contents produce the same token; different contents may produce the same token due to a hash collision. A collision can suppress an update until a subsequent snapshot produces a different token, or until the client requests a full snapshot with token -1. This is accepted for diagnostic information; a periodic refresh is not added.

Fixing the describe output. Describing a group configuration returns the stored value, not the effective one. That is related but separate: it does not reach the client. KAFKA-20835 addresses another consequence of a stored override outside the current bounds, namely that altering any other configuration of the group fails validation until the stale override is fixed; it does not change what the client sees.

Updating client behavior from the reported values. Out of scope, and it would need its own KIP. The values are reported for logging only.
